facts.text: Wallingford sits on a ridge that climbs from Lake Union to North 45th Street, giving it sweeping views of both the Olympic and Cascade mountains.
The neighborhood’s name comes from a 19th‑century homestead on the hill, and its streets were laid out as a classic streetcar suburb in the 1920s.
Gas Works Park, a former gasification plant turned public park, is a landmark that locals and visitors alike enjoy for its industrial history and panoramic lake views.
Historic Wallingford, founded in 2017, is a volunteer group that preserves the neighborhood’s heritage through walking tours, oral histories, and a dedicated website.
In 2023 Historic Wallingford helped secure the Wallingford‑Meridian Streetcar Historic District’s listing on the National Register of Historic Places.
The Wallingford Branch of the Seattle Public Library, located next to the Solid Ground food bank, serves as a community hub for learning and support services.
